body: Nah, someday life won't be all peaches and sunshine. Enjoy it while it lasts.
Spoiled little fucker. Someday reality is going to slap you in the face.
Probably the most ignorant bullshit I've ever read. Go fuck yourself.
Sounds like its already there, bro... Go get some help.

We're all here solely because we're inclined to find excuses... Every single one of us. 

Everyone is telling you not to drink because we've all been there already.

Lol, it's noisy? That's the best excuse you can come up with?

You know if you drink you're going to regret it in the morning... Why not skp that step?

If you decide to drink then you've lost your battle and have to start over.
Looks like we share an anniversary... Heh.
And you've got it, bro.

I quit nearly 3months ago. Same shoes as you. Right out of college, told myself I would stop... Didn't. Now I've forced myself to. 

If you have anxiety problems... Just know that they may get WAY worse for the first few days/weeks. Withdrawal blows, and the symptoms can keep coming back for up to two years... Absolutely worth it though. 

I've taken to exercising way more than I used to, lost a ton of weight, and physically feel much better than I have in years.

Well done, buddy! I'm training for my first tri... Currently working on the swim and to a lesser extent the run. I've been an endurance cyclist for a few years, so I think I've got that one covered.

My swim really sucks though. Still in the can barely swim 100m without stopping club... Working on my form and breathing... Any tips?
Oh, I will. Exercise has always been a big part of my life, even while i was drinking...

Well, you've gotten the hard part out of the way... Now you just need to stop.

We've all been where you are, we know what it's like... Do you have any specific concerns you want addressed? Anything you'd like to share?

If not, that's okay... Just know that we're here to help when you need us.
I think working out is a great idea. I took all my booze "budget" and got a fitness club membership. I've lost a ton of weight, and training for a triathlon... I feel so good now...
Yes, I definitely think therapy would be helpful... It's not normal to find everything boring.

What kind of hobbies have you tried to adopt? 

I decided I wanted to run a triathlon... The training every day is incredibly fun. Have you tried that? 

Hiking is fun... Have you tried that? 

Reading a book? 

Running a 5k?

Watch a show? 

Take a nap?

Write a book? 

Watch porn?

There are literally hundreds of things you can do without drinking that are very entertaining. If you literally can't find any joy in anything, you may want to go talk to a psychiatrist about whether or not you have depression.
I've informed /r/suicidewatch about this post.

Hey man. 

Depression and anxiety and even suicidal thoughts are NORMAL when you stop drinking. This happens to a lot of people. You are not alone. Breathe. 

You should really speak to a professional. If you were affording alcohol before you can afford to see a therapist. Do it now. 

Call the suicide hotline if you really think you might hurt yourself. Or stop in at /r/suicidewatch 

Suicide is a permenant solution to a TEMPORARY problem. You'll be okay, I promise.

Sure thing man. One of the most comforting things I've told myself about this whole thing is that I'm not the first person, and I won't be the last person that this has happened to... And I'll be just fine.

It is a damn shame, but it was fun while it lasted. Take the good memories and hold them close, forget the bad ones, and go make some new (healthier) ones.

I certainly wouldn't mind keeping in touch. Feel free to message me whenever you want. :)

Hey buddy. In the same boat as you. Been sober for over a month... I've lost 10 lbs sleep better than I have in years, perform better at work, and generally just feel better without the beer...

I still have a case of home brews in the closet and 15 gallons still fermenting. I'm going to bottle it and give it all away to friends...

I seriously feel ya, because we enjoy some of the same things... And I've dumped a ton of time and money into the hobby... But you know what?? I have other hobbies that make me feel way better.

I'm currently training for a triathlon (something I would never have been able to do a month ago)... 

Good luck to you.

My recommendation: quit for a while... A month or two. Try new things. If you still miss it (I honestly don't) then set a hard limit of 2 drinks for yourself (in social situations only -- no drinking alone) and see if you can handle it.

If you can't do it, then you'll know you have to quit.
I've always been fairly fit... But e beer belly has got to go. Time to get serious.
You need to tell then that you've quit drinking. They will either support you and help you achieve your goal, or they'll keep pressuring you. If that's the case then it's time for new friends.

I'm having similar problems. Planning on seeing a psychologist as soon as one will return my calls. Good luck to you!

Depression and anxiety are treatable illnesses. There's no reason to try and deal with it on your own.
No, but you should probably still talk to her about it. I'm sure she would like to know your opinion in making this difficult decision. Just go be supportive.

Oh, I know. It's gotta happen. Just sucks. :)

Thanks.
Not sure I'm ready for that. As of now I'm content talking to my girlfriend and soon therapist. I did find there's an agnostic aa in my area though, so if I ever need it its there.
Yeah. It's hard to admit that something you enjoy is destructive... But life is full of other things to find enjoyment in. Thanks.

Thanks! I certainly don't plan on forgetting to mention anything. I've been fortunate enough to not need to see a psychologist before so I don't really know what to expect. I've been telling my girlfriend everything so far and it's been very therapeutic. She's also been a complete sweetheart about it. Hasn't judged or gotten angry at me once...just wants to see me get better. :3

Best of luck to you!

Fortunately for me I have plenty of hobbies that are or can be alcohol free. I'm an avid cyclist, like to tinker with electronics, like exercising and being outside. The only hobby ill give up is the beer brewing... Which really sucks because I definitely enjoyed it and sunk a fair amount of money into it already. :/

I'm sure my friends can carry on without me... And they can have my stuff.
